languageClaims.sourceType: Elite Fourum collector guide + Bulbapedia + manufacturer/regional catalog cross-check
languageClaims.evidence: The Elite Fourum language matrix lists ordinary Hidden Fates Eevee 49/68 in English, French, German, Italian, Spanish and Portuguese, but the Battle Academy 2020 Mewtwo Deck stamped Eevee 49/68 only in English, French, German and Italian. The same four-language scope is shown for the Charizard Deck stamp. Bulbapedia's Battle Academy 2020 article lists French, German and Italian product releases and includes Snorlax 50/68 in the Mewtwo Deck: https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Battle_Academy_2020_%28TCG%29. Spanish records point to later or inconsistent products: BoardGameGeek (https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgameversion/614262/spanish-edition) and Raccoon Games (https://www.raccoongames.es/es/producto/pokemon-tcg-academia-de-combate) describe Cinderace V/Pikachu V/Eevee V, while SafariZone describes Battle Academy 2024. Portuguese records likewise identify Copag's later Cinderace/Pikachu/Eevee product (https://copag.com.br/pokemon/blog/detalhes/box-academia-de-batalha-novos-decks-para-iniciantes), Copag reference 31495/EAN 7896192314949, and a Portuguese-market listing that warns the article may be Castilian, English or Catalan rather than Portuguese. No Spanish or Portuguese BA20 MWT Snorlax card image, product code/EAN, manufacturer record, or localized listing was found. The ordinary Spanish Hidden Fates Snorlax 50/68 is unstamped and does not establish a BA20 MWT printing. Cardmarket's language filter is marketplace metadata, not a print manifest. The Spanish and Portuguese claims are therefore contradicted. Language-specific conclusion: no Spanish BA20 MWT Snorlax printing was found.

languageClaims.sourceType: Bulbapedia (fan wiki), product article, exclusivity statement + half-deck list
languageClaims.evidence: Bulbapedia's National Beginning Set (TCG) states the product's exclusivity outright: "The National Pokédex Beginning Set (Japanese: はじめてセット 全国図鑑版セット) is a Japanese-exclusive Half Deck Deck Kit released in the BW era of the Pokémon Trading Card Game." Its DeckInfobox carries one unqualified release, April 20, 2012, and the article has no "In other languages" section. The half-deck list carries this card — "Halfdecklist/nmentry|027/034|National Beginning Set|Snorlax|27|Colorless||1" — so the source reaches the card and not only the product. A Japanese-exclusive product has no Korean printing. RATIONALE REPLACED 2026-08-10: this replaces the era-format argument from "Pokémon in South Korea" that the row previously cited. That argument covers the window between the DP and Black & White eras, and Black & White launched in Japan on 2010-12-17 against this product's 2012-04-20 — it did not reach this card, as the scope correction of 2026-08-10 recorded. The verdict was never the problem; the rationale was, and it is replaced rather than the verdict retracted. This is not an absence argument: "Japanese-exclusive" is a source asserting what exists, the same character as the closed enumeration that carries the pre-DP Korean rows, and rule 3 governs a source that fails to mention something. A search for positive Korean evidence was run first at the owner's direction and found none: koreanpokemoncards.com returns nothing for Snorlax and pokumon carries no Beginning Set entry in any language. Retrieved 2026-08-10.

Simplified Chinese 卡比兽 HP 150, 特性 贪嘴, 厚重压制 130, Illus. HYOGONOSUKE, G regulation mark, 151C 143/151 U, ©2025. A Master Ball pattern is visible in the reflective foil across the card body outside the artwork. Retained as SPEC-0683.

The official guide states that cards of rarity R and above are foil cards produced with mirror (镜面) processing, which is the Western holo, and that Simplified Chinese C, U and R cards can be pulled as the locality-specific patterned random foil treatment, a reverse holo. The collection owner fixed this terminology on 2026-11-03 (#438). It does not state that these are the only printings.

Complete seller photograph of Japanese R団のカビゴンex HP100, ダークヒーラー, どくのつめ 20 and たおれこむ 60, Illus.Mitsuhiro Arita, printed 062/084 with the R set mark. Holographic sparkle crosses the artwork and frame. Listing title: '[1EDあり] ポケモンカード R団のカビゴンex (062/084) / ロケット団の逆襲'. Retained as SPEC-0639.

Close-up of the lower left of the same R団のカビゴンex from the same listing: 弱点 with the fighting icon, ZM7-1S9-JGF and the holo border; a printed 1 EDITION mark stands immediately left of ZM7-1S9-JGF. Retained as SPEC-0640.

Complete seller photograph of a second Japanese R団のカビゴンex 062/084 copy (Illus.Mitsuhiro Arita, holo sparkle). The dark 1 EDITION mark stands at the lower left immediately left of ZM7-1S9-JGF. Listing title: 'ポケモンカード 062/084 ★ 1ED R団のカビゴンex (31)'. Retained as SPEC-0641.

Full owner photograph captured 2025-05-24 of Japanese R団のカビゴンex PCG3 062/084, HP 100, in a clear magnetic holder. Sparkling holo points and coloured reflection are visible across the artwork and card frame. SPEC-0096 and SPEC-0097 are alternate views of this same card. The 1 EDITION mark position left of ZM7-1S9-JGF at the lower left is visibly empty on the complete, legible card face (position confirmed against 1st Edition copies SPEC-0640/0641), which establishes the Unlimited printing (owner rule 2026-10-22). Retained as SPEC-0095.

Second full owner photograph captured 2025-05-24 of the same Japanese R団のカビゴンex PCG3 062/084 card. Alternate lighting again shows sparkling holo points across the artwork and frame. Retained as SPEC-0096.
Closer owner photograph captured 2025-05-24 of the same Japanese PCG3 062/084 Rocket's Snorlax ex. The name, number and holo sparkle are clear; no additional card is inferred. Retained as SPEC-0097.
